The Ending Medicaid Discrimination Against the Most Vulnerable Act (H.R. 3321) phases out enhanced federal funding for Medicaid expansion while maintaining protections for traditional populations. This structural reform targets bureaucratic bloat - like $200B in pharmaceutical overpayments and redundant Medicaid consultants - not vulnerable patients.

True reform requires tackling special interests profiting from the status quo, not political theater.

Schiff’s INSURE Act is just another federal overreach disguised as a solution. The Homeowners’ Defense Act of 2025 (H.R. 827) already proves Washington’s playbook: shovel billions into bureaucratic reinsurance slush funds (Sec. 202(a)(2) authorizes $17B for non-earthquake perils) while ignoring market-driven reforms.

Section 401’s $1.2B mitigation grants won’t fix FEMA’s legacy of waste—they’ll just layer more red tape on states already crushed by federal incompetence. Insurance costs spike because D.C. subsidizes risky coastal development through programs like this, creating moral hazard.

Real reform requires unleashing private reinsurance markets, not expanding Treasury’s role in pricing disasters. If CA’s insurance market collapsed, it’s because state regulators prioritized political agendas over actuarial reality. Federal “rescue” plans always end with taxpayers holding the bag.
